cells.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that for certain revenue-producing employees in its Wealth Management and Investment Management business segments, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link employee compensation to revenues.
items.quote: For certain revenue-producing employees in the Wealth Management and Investment Management business segments, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link employee compensation to revenues.
items.scope: Wealth Management and Investment Management business segments

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that its Wealth Management compensation and benefits expenses increased primarily due to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors driven by higher compensable revenue.
items.quote: Compensation and benefits expenses increased, primarily due to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors driven by higher compensable revenue.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that a Financial Advisor serviced through a Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisor is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus and does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee.
items.quote: If your account is serviced through a Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisor ("MSVA"), your MSVA is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus and does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that the amount of the client fee is a factor used in calculating Financial Advisor compensation, and that if the fee rate is below a certain threshold the advisor is given credit for less than the total amount of the fee.
items.quote: The amount of the fee you pay is a factor we use in calculating the compensation we pay your Financial Advisor... If your fee rate is below a certain threshold, we give your Financial Advisor credit for less than the total amount of your fee in calculating his or her compensation.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that Financial Advisors in advisory programs do not receive additional compensation as a result of the support fees, mutual fund administrative service fees and data analytics payments received by Morgan Stanley.
items.quote: Financial Advisors in advisory programs do not receive additional compensation as a result of the support fees, mutual fund administrative service fees and data analytics payments received by Morgan Stanley.

items.text: Trade press reports that Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors must generate that much more revenue to receive the same pay next year.
items.quote: As it has in the past, Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

cells.reason: Morgan Stanley discloses a formulaic payout structure linking advisor pay to revenues and specific elements (MSVA salary+bonus, a fee threshold, no extra comp from certain fees), and trade press reports a 10% threshold increase, but no specific numeric payout grid or rate is published.
